literature_clarification.original_locations: 2017-12-28 author manuscript, PDF pages 3 and 13, footnote 5, and Figure A2 caption on PDF page 70
literature_clarification.original_event: T-4 is the latest sale close for the example of cash paid to recipients on the morning of T: T+3 settlement supplies cash by T-1 close. It is not the beginning of the selling interval. The text separately allows T+1 payment obligations to extend sales to T-3, with liquidity/risk considerations moving some selling earlier.
literature_clarification.later_locations: 2026-06-08 main text section 5, footnotes 23-24; appendix IA.17
literature_clarification.later_event: The later paper calls tau-5/tau-4/tau-3 the marginal cash-raising boundary under T+3/T+2/T+1. These are not the starting days of its six-day PreTOM interval. Footnote 23 relates boundaries to the full-sample smoothed interval; the reform test concerns adjacent boundary-day relocation.
literature_clarification.resolved: The discrepancy is not a start-versus-end comparison or a different month-end zero point. Both use the last trading day as T/tau and discuss a marginal/latest selling boundary.
literature_clarification.unresolved: The examined text does not supply a common recipient-payment deadline or an explicit additional processing/custody buffer that maps the original T-4 under T+3 to the later tau-5 under T+3.
literature_clarification.inference_not_source_fact: If all intervening days were ordinary settlement days, a T+3 sale at tau-5 supplies cash at tau-2, whereas a sale at T-4 supplies cash at T-1. An additional one-day cash buffer could reconcile these, but that buffer is not established by the examined documents and must not be invented or selected from return peaks.

decision: Retain the single settlement-cash deadline mechanism as a backup needs_source lead. Do not select either absolute offset, add an empirical PreTOM window, generate the proposed indicator or start a backtest.
minimum_remaining_condition: A dated institutional recipient-payment obligation together with its bank/custodian cash-funding cutoff and applicable ordinary-equity CNS/banking-day exception rules must determine one explicit deadline. A one-day buffer inferred from the external return profile is insufficient. Existing 2026 anticipated DTC notice and the limited indexed holiday leads do not complete the historical calendar.
